title: Checkout function reference
audience: Developers calling the prepared checkout function
purpose: Describe the guest gate and returned dictionaries without claiming HTTP reachability.
scope: checkout(user, items) in the prepared legacy fixture; server binding is outside scope.

sections.title: Inputs and assumptions
sections.content:
The function receives user and items. It reads the guest_checkout setting when user is falsey.

The function does not validate item structure.

rows: A truthy user bypasses the guest gate.
Returned as order on the successful branch.

sections.title: Successful result
sections.content: The successful branch returns status 200, the supplied items as order, and requires_login false.

sections.title: Guest denied
sections.content: An absent user with guest checkout disabled receives status 401 and requires_login true.

sections.title: Side effects and boundaries
sections.content: The checkout body reads settings and constructs a result. It does not persist an order; settings implementation and external callers require separate inspection.

examples.title: Guest gate example
examples.code:
from checkout import checkout
from settings import save_checkout_settings

save_checkout_settings(False)
result = checkout(None, [])
assert result['status'] == 401
if result['status'] == 401:
    assert result['requires_login'] is True
examples.prerequisites: An authorized Python fixture environment with checkout.py and settings.py on the module path; modifying this fixture setting is permitted there.
examples.expected: A dictionary containing status 401 and requires_login true.
